question: Which Linux companion-app track, if any, should become OpenClaw's official path now that Windows Hub is documented and released?
rationale: Current main resolves much of the Windows side but still lacks Linux app code, and the open Linux PRs propose different architectures with security, packaging, proof, and ownership tradeoffs that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Keep umbrella and pick Linux track
options.body: Maintain this issue while reviewing the open Linux PRs for architecture, security, packaging, and proof before choosing a canonical path.

options.title: Split Linux into a narrower tracker
options.body: Create a dedicated Linux companion issue that preserves the remaining scope and linked implementation candidates, then narrow this umbrella around shipped Windows context.

options.title: Defer official Linux app
options.body: If maintainers decide Linux should stay community-owned for now, close only after posting a clear policy and external-app handoff.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and pick Linux track
recommendation.body: Maintain this issue while reviewing the open Linux PRs for architecture, security, packaging, and proof before choosing a canonical path.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the issue, gave the clearest Linux product-direction comments, and maintains the current platform status docs.
